name: United Arab Bank
founded: 1975 (incorporated in Sharjah as a private joint stock company; converted to a public company in 1982)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. The Commercial Bank (P.S.Q.C.) of Qatar is the largest shareholder with 39.91% at 31 Dec 2025, a stake first acquired (40%) in December 2007, and appoints 4 of 11 directors. Other holders above 5% at 31 Dec 2025: Al Majid Investment Company 10.79%, HH Sheikh Mohammed bin Faisal bin Sultan Al Qassimi (Chairman) 9.99% and Sheikh Faisal bin Sultan bin Salem Al Qassimi 7.42%. No change of control found in 2026 filings or news (checked 2026-10-12).

shareholders.holder: HH Sheikh Mohammed bin Faisal bin Sultan Al Qassimi
Sheikh Faisal bin Sultan bin Salem Al Qassimi

government_link: No UAE government shareholder found among holders above 5% (31 Dec 2025). The largest shareholder, The Commercial Bank (Qatar), is itself a listed Qatari bank. Members of the Sharjah ruling family (Al Qassimi) hold 17.41% combined, and the Chairman is one of them (S3).
group_structure: Single bank, no subsidiaries reported. Islamic banking runs through a Shari'a-compliant window at selected branches, with Islamic financing receivables of AED 3.02bn gross at 30 Jun 2026 (S1). UAB is an associate of The Commercial Bank (Qatar) (universe id qa-cbq), which equity-accounts its 39.91% stake, so UAB figures would be partly double-counted if added to CBQ's.
footprint: UAE only. 6 branches and 22 ATMs at end 2025 (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah) (S3). Three mall branches were planned for early 2026; a branch at Dalma Mall, Abu Dhabi, opened in June 2026 (S11).
customer_segments: Corporate and commercial (main business), personal banking (mass retail via salary-transfer loans, mortgages and cards; Premium Banking for affluent clients), Islamic banking window, treasury clients.
business_lines: Corporate Banking; Treasury & Capital Markets; Personal Banking (accounts, cards, personal loans, mortgages, deposits, Premium Banking); Islamic Banking window (Wakala/Mudaraba deposits, Murabaha financing). Personal Banking contributed 10% of FY2025 operating income (AED 79m) with AED 3.1bn of loans and AED 3.0bn of deposits at 31 Dec 2025 (S3). Retail investment products are limited to term deposits, treasury FX and rate hedging, in-app ADX IPO subscription (Aug 2025) and third-party market access promised to Premium clients.

capabilities.wealth_summary: UAB is a mid-sized, corporate-led Sharjah bank (AED 27.7bn assets at 30 Jun 2026) whose Personal Banking unit is only about 10% of income and is built around loans, cards and deposits. Its affluent offer is Premium Banking: a dedicated licensed relationship manager, lounges, preferential pricing, and claimed access to local, regional and international markets 'through leading investment firms', private equity deals, Lombard lending and succession planning; no thresholds or named providers are published. The 'Wealth Management' web section is treasury-run and lists term deposits, FX and rate hedging, and Islamic Wakala/Mudaraba deposits; no funds, bonds, structured notes or discretionary mandates are shown. In Aug 2025 it added ADX IPO subscription in its mobile app, and the annual report 2025 says Personal Banking will introduce 'virtual assets and equities' and strengthen Premium Banking from 2026.

asset_management.detail: No asset management subsidiary, own funds or AUM disclosed.

brokerage.detail: No own brokerage licence or subsidiary found. Premium page claims market access through unnamed third-party investment firms. ADX IPO subscription in-app since Aug 2025 is primary-market only. Equities are planned for 2026 (annual report).

digital_investing.detail: Limited: UAB mobile app supports ADX IPO subscriptions (from 21 Aug 2025) and conventional and Islamic term deposit journeys (2025). Revamped app launched 2025 with 80+ services; Lune AI insights partnership (Jul 2025). Equities and virtual assets planned for 2026.

advisory.detail: Premium page says licensed RMs risk-profile clients and build 'personalised, dynamic wealth management solutions'; no advisory product, fee or licence detail found.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: None found on website or in annual report.

funds_platform.detail: No mutual fund shelf shown; the Investment Solutions page lists only deposit products.

structured_products.detail: Treasury pages offer FX options, bespoke derivative strategies and structured interest-rate hedges (hedging, not investment notes). No retail structured notes found.

private_markets.detail: Premium page claims 'access to exclusive private equity deals'; no named vehicle or provider.

islamic_wealth.detail: Islamic window: Wakala and Mudaraba deposits (incl. Golden Visa Wakala, Islamic Enhanced Escalator), Islamic profit-rate swaps. Premium page says Shari'ah-compliant wealth solutions are available. Islamic banking assets crossed AED 3.5bn in 2025.

opportunities: Annual report 2025 states Personal Banking will introduce virtual assets and equities and strengthen Premium Banking from 2026, with no execution or product partner named yet (S3).
Current retail 'Wealth Management' shelf is deposits plus treasury hedging; no funds, model portfolios, discretionary or structured notes found (S8, S19).
Premium Banking already promises market access, private equity deals and Lombard lending through unnamed third parties, so a product shelf by API would fill a stated promise (S7).
Mobile app was rebuilt in 2025 and already hosts ADX IPO subscription and Lune AI insights, showing willingness to plug in partners (S3, S9, S10).
barriers: Retail is small: Personal Banking was 10% of FY2025 operating income (AED 79m) and the bank is corporate-led (S3).
Strategic decisions are influenced by a 39.91% foreign bank shareholder (The Commercial Bank, Qatar) with 4 board seats (S3).
Personal Banking leadership changed in 2026 and is not yet confirmed (S6, S14).
